purpose: RFC-2026-016 closed the direction of DATA-DEC-03 and refused to claim the control, because the service path was undecided and on Supabase the service-role key bypasses RLS. The instance was then measured: service_role bypasses, and so does postgres, which is the role in every direct connection string -- so both obvious options bypass. postgres holds rolcreaterole, so a topology that does not bypass is implementable. This package records the decision that follows, which closes the half of DATA-DEC-03 that was left open.

include: RFC-2026-017 recording the service-path decision and the role topology it implies
The measurement behind it, taken from the provisioned instance rather than vendor documentation
The costs of the decision, recorded so they are not discovered later as surprises
exclude: Creating the roles. That is a migration, and it belongs to the batch A0 owns, not to a decision record.
Writing any tenant table or policy. Batch 010 is A1 Identity's.
Claiming the isolation is proven. No tenant table exists, so no cross-tenant assertion has run.
Disposing this RFC. That is the Product Owner's act on a disposition branch.

amends_without_owning.rationale: THIS INCREMENT AMENDS NOTHING OUTSIDE THIS PACKAGE. It corrects three sentences in this package's own open_blockers and removes one that is spent, touching only the manifest and the handoff this package owns. `paths` is emptied rather than left carrying the earlier increment's four (evidence/VERIFICATION.md, scripts/test-suite-contract.mjs, test-kits/branch-identity.test.mjs, test-kits/integrity-manifest.json), because verify-branch-scope reads the declaration in both directions and exits 74 on a declared pattern matching nothing in the diff. `recorded_on` is removed with them: it named work-packages/WP-0A-A0-002.json as the register where the amendment was recorded, that register's `ownership.amended_by` has never held an entry for this package, and with `paths` empty there is no amendment for it to point at. Those four paths remain in git history.

acceptance_criteria: The RFC states the measurement it rests on, names the instance it was taken from, and does not cite vendor documentation in its place.
It records that postgres bypasses RLS as well as service_role, so that a reader does not conclude a direct driver is by itself a fix.
The role topology names every role, its purpose, and that none holds BYPASSRLS.
The costs are recorded in the RFC, not left to be discovered during implementation.
The RFC does NOT claim tenant isolation is proven, and names the assertion that would prove it as still owed.
The RFC is committed with status Proposed.
required_tests: The work-package and ownership validators accept this manifest
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. RFC-2026-017 is a Proposed decision record: no role is created, no policy written, no migration applied, and nothing on the provisioned instance is touched by it.
open_blockers: WHAT RFC-2026-017 §7 ASKS FOR NOW EXISTS AND RUNS, AND WHETHER THAT DISCHARGES §7 IS NOT THIS PACKAGE'S TO DECIDE. §7 asks for "the service identity attempting an operation the matrix marks `N` for service and being denied with an ERROR, not an empty result", and says it "does not exist yet". Re-measured 2026-10-07 at 4dd767d (main after PR #200), by importing buildCases from tests/db/identity/isolation-cases.mjs: 1200 cases are built; 61 declare `covers: ['RFC-2026-017§7', ...]`, of which 20 expect `denied`, 39 `no-rows` and 2 `no-effect`; the 20 denials are over 20 distinct app tables, of 62 the migrations create. (At 5abee8b this blocker counted 65 blocks and 28 denials statically; the drop is recorded and its cause, labels removed where the static suite refused them, is named by comments in the same file, e.g. "NOT labelled `RFC-2026-017§7`, and the label was on it until the static suite refused it"; evidence/WP-0A-A0-008/author-self-check-2026-10-07.md §4.) tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs still carries the test named "the service denial is attributable to row level security and not to a forgotten grant"; and private.as_service() in db/foundation/test-helpers/auth-context.sql still reaches app_worker through `set_config('role','app_worker',true)` and checks it landed. So the assertion exists, runs, and runs as a role that does not bypass. THIS BLOCKER IS LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: closing it would be this package judging its own §7 condition met, and an independent reviewer should decide whether 20 denial cases over 20 of 62 tables, beside 39 cases that expect an empty result, are what §7 meant.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNPROVEN IS THE PRODUCTION SERVICE PATH, NOT THE POLICY LAYER, AND THE GAP IS NARROWER THAN IT WAS (corrected 2026-10-07, evidence/WP-0A-A0-008/author-self-check-2026-10-07.md §4). The tests above become app_worker from a superuser connection, which works because postgres may SET ROLE to anything. Until 2026-10-05 this blocker went on: RFC-2026-022 §5/8 measures that the only MEMBER of app_worker is postgres, and RFC-2026-019 §4/3 leaves app_worker's connection method undecided, so nothing outside a test helper can be app_worker. That connection method is decided now: RFC-2026-028 (Approved 2026-10-05) gives the worker a login role, app_worker_login, whose one membership is app_worker with INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE, ADMIN FALSE, and db/foundation/migrations/173_worker_login_identity.sql, on main, creates it on migrate-clean clusters. RFC-2026-022 §5/8's measurement describes the tree before 173 and is history. WHAT IS STILL OPEN is what RFC-2026-028's own header names, among them (not exhaustive; read that header as a whole): 173 is declared NOT applied to the provisioned instance until Q-028-13 and Q170-c are measured there; credential custody (Q-028-3) has no named owner; the platform pooler (Q-028-12) is unmeasured; the production runner's checks (A1R-2, widened by A1-173-1) are owed to RFC-2026-026's worker half; and A1's acceptance as DATA-DEC-03's co-owner is owed. 173's own header adds that it writes no policy, so app_worker reads and writes no row of any forced table, through that role or any other, until each service cell's batch lands one. No case in the isolation suite connects AS app_worker_login. So the production service path is still unproven, and it is owed to RFC-2026-028's open items and RFC-2026-026's worker half, not to this package.
